W: Earth walls, shored up with old fence posts. Somebody dug this by hand, a spoonful a night.
B: The open-hand banner of the Hales, hung where no guard will ever see it. It has been mended with turnip sacking, very carefully.
t: A map of Kaldorhold, weighted down with turnips. Pebbles mark the guard posts. In the corner, in a careful hand: WHEN HE COMES BACK.
L: A list of names, the rebellion's, written in code. The code is very simple. It's mostly turnips.
2: The ladder back up to the weaver's cottage.

objects.name: Mira
lines: ...You're not a guard. Fen sent you down, didn't he. Fen trusts everybody. It's his worst quality and his best one.

answer: The only room in Osric's Rest the king's guards don't know about.
Upstairs, we farm and we pray. Down here, we plan.
The day the prince comes home. Brannoc. Osric's boy.
Everyone up there believes he's coming back. Somebody has to have a plan for when he does. That's us.
The king doesn't age. Five hundred years. The horde says he casts no shadow.
Everybody casts a shadow. Somebody's lying.
Because I'm small, and the horde isn't.
You don't have to be the biggest. You have to practise every day until you're the steadiest.

questions.ask: A rebellion of turnip farmers? He'll crush you.
answer: He might.
But he'd have to come down here to do it, and the ceiling's very low. We've thought about this.

lines: You did it. I'm going home.

objects.name: Sergeant Holt
lines: We didn't run. We relocated. Bravely.
Now we're planning to relocate the king. Same principle. Longer way round.

answer: Sergeant Holt. My great-great-great-grandfather served in the Lecrest Second, the prince's own regiment.
When the shadow came, they walked out of the war rather than fight it. They got as far as here, and stopped.
Kaldorhold. Every guard post, every gate, every place the drawbridge chain could slip.
Five hundred years of notes. The pebbles are guards. The turnip is the king. It's a big turnip.
Because one day you'll have to stand your ground, and it'll be too late to start training then.
Ask me how I know.
The old war, the one that never was. Every forge in the land beat out blades for the old king, and the other seven kingdoms sharpened theirs.
Then nobody marched. Soldiers, waiting for the right moment. Sound familiar?

questions.ask: Relocated? You ran, you old coward.
answer: We ran with purpose.
...The purpose was not being there. But it was a purpose.

lines: We're going back. Bravely. Slightly behind everyone else, but bravely.
Somebody take down the sign. It's a deserters' camp now. Was. Ex-deserters'.
